name: Stripe Atlas
description: Stripe Atlas is a self-service company-formation product for Delaware entities, EIN acquisition, founder equity, legal documents, 83(b) elections, registered-agent service, banking, and startup resources.
agentUseSummary: Stripe Atlas cannot currently be connected as a distinct Relay agent provider because Stripe documents Atlas as an interactive Dashboard application and publishes no Atlas API endpoints, delegated Atlas scopes, webhooks, remote MCP tools, or service credentials. Stripe's general payments and financial-infrastructure APIs do not grant authority over Atlas formation, founder, EIN, equity, legal-document, or 83(b) workflows. Relay will not reuse a Stripe session, broaden an existing Stripe key, or infer Atlas operations from Dashboard behavior.

blocked.label: Connect Stripe Atlas
blocked.description: Stripe publishes no supported Atlas-specific OAuth scope, API key, remote MCP, webhook, or other delegated account contract for Relay to implement.

blocked.label: Broaden Stripe API authority
blocked.description: General Stripe API keys, Stripe Apps OAuth, restricted keys, payment APIs, and Stripe MCP tools must not be treated as authority over Atlas applications or legal workflows.

blocked.label: Perform Atlas legal or tax actions
blocked.description: Company formation, Delaware filings, founder equity issuance, IP contribution, EIN applications, 83(b) elections, document execution, registered-agent changes, SAFE workflows, and banking applications are blocked.

blocked.label: Use unsupported automation
blocked.description: Relay will not automate the Atlas Dashboard, reuse browser sessions, capture founder identity or tax data, scrape documents, reverse-engineer private endpoints, or impersonate signatures or consent.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled without a supported Atlas-specific API or remote MCP contract with stable schemas and narrowly delegated authority.

runtimeSupport.description: No Atlas-specific customer-authenticated operation is available to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No Atlas-specific customer-authenticated operation is available to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Stripe documents Atlas through an interactive application and Dashboard. The public Atlas materials define company-formation, EIN, founder-equity, legal-document, 83(b), registered-agent, banking, and SAFE workflows but no Atlas API resources, scopes, webhooks, remote MCP tools, service credentials, sandbox contract, or revocation semantics. Stripe's separately documented developer APIs and app permissions cover Stripe platform resources and cannot be broadened by inference to Atlas legal authority.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not expose an Atlas Connect flow, request Stripe keys for Atlas, publish Atlas runtime tools, automate the Dashboard, or capture founder identity/tax data. Reconsider only if Stripe publishes an Atlas-specific supported API or remote MCP contract with stable schemas, explicit least-privilege permissions, sandbox behavior, revocation, audit semantics, and human confirmation for legal and tax actions.

evidence.supports: Stripe documents Atlas as a self-service company-formation product that incorporates Delaware entities, obtains EINs, initiates founder equity, files 83(b) elections, executes legal documents, supplies registered-agent service, and enables banking and SAFE workflows. The page publishes no callable Atlas API or MCP contract.

Stripe documents an interactive Atlas application collecting legal names, parent-company and tax identifiers, founder identity and birth data, SSN/ITIN, home addresses, ownership, roles, signatures, and company details before Atlas files documents, obtains an EIN, and issues shares. These are consequential legal and identity workflows.

Stripe's public developer resources separately document SDKs, API keys, Stripe Apps, payments and financial APIs, event destinations, agent tooling, and Stripe MCP. No Atlas API resource or permission is documented; Relay therefore does not infer Atlas authority from general Stripe developer credentials.

The Atlas agreement begins when founders submit an Atlas application and grants Stripe permission to form a Delaware company, appoint a registered agent, and obtain an EIN. Relay will not submit or accept those legal commitments through an undocumented autonomous interface.
